blocks.text: his companions. When I again looked at Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) (after he had been listening awhile), I saw that tears were flowing from his eyes."[^1]
Hadhrat Ubayd bin Umayr (RA) once recited the verse:

blocks.arabic_text: فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جِئْنَا مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍۭ بِشَهِيْدٍ وَّجِئْنَا بِكَ عَلٰى هٰٓؤُلَاءِ شَهِيْدًا
blocks.text: How will it be (the condition of the Kuffaar on the Day of Qiyaamah) when We shall bring forth a witness from every nation (the Ambiyaa of every community who will testify against the Kuffaar) and call you (O Muhammad ﷺ) to be a witness over all of them?

(Upon hearing this verse) Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) started weeping so profusely that his beard and collar became wet with tears. Hadhrat Abdullaah says, "The man sitting beside Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said to me, 'I actually contemplated getting up and telling Hadhrat Ubayd bin Umayr (RA) to curtail his talk because of the difficulty he was causing the elderly man (Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA)).'"[^2]
The Weeping of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) and Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA)

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Mulaykah says, "I accompanied Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) from Makkah to Madinah and wherever he set up camp, he stood in salaah for half the night." When Hadhrat Ayyoob asked him what Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA)'s recitation of the Qur'aan was like, he replied, "He once cried painfully as he continuously recited the following verse with slow intonation:

blocks.arabic_text: وَجَآءَتْ سَكْرَةُ الْمَوْتِ بِالْحَقِّ ۗ ذٰلِكَ مَا كُنْتَ مِنْهُ تَحِيْدُ
blocks.text: The pangs (agony) of death will bring the truth (of Imaan to every person). (It will then be said to the dying person,) "This (death) is what you used to avoid (However, now you have no option)."[^3]
Hadhrat Abu Rajaa (RA) says, "The lines on the face of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) where his tears ran resembled two old shoe straps."[^4]

Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Abu Saudah says that he once saw Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) on the wall of the Masjid that (Allaah showed Rasulullaah ﷺ a vantage point that) overlooked a valley of Jahannam.
